title: Measurement Properties — Reliability, Validity, Responsiveness and MDC vs MCID

hook.en: A goniometer reads 45 degrees today and 52 tomorrow. Did the patient improve, or is the tool noisy? Before you trust any measure, you need to know how reliable, valid and responsive it is, and how much change is real and how much is just measurement noise.
hook.ur: Goniometer aaj 45 degree aur kal 52 degree batata hai. Kya mareez behtar hua, ya aala shor wala hai? Kisi bhi naap par bharosa se pehle aap ko jaanna chahiye ke woh kitna reliable, valid aur responsive hai, aur kitni tabdeeli asal hai aur kitni sirf naap ka shor.

goal.en: By the end, you'll tell reliability from validity and responsiveness, read ICC and kappa values, explain SEM and the minimal detectable change (MDC), and separate MDC from the minimal clinically important difference (MCID).
goal.ur: End tak aap reliability ko validity aur responsiveness se alag karenge, ICC aur kappa ki values parhenge, SEM aur minimal detectable change (MDC) samjhayenge, aur MDC ko minimal clinically important difference (MCID) se alag karenge.

text.en: **Reliability** is consistency: does the measure give the same answer when nothing has changed (same person on different days, or different raters)? **Validity** is accuracy of meaning: does it measure what it claims to measure? **Responsiveness** is the ability to detect real change over time. The **COSMIN** initiative sets standards for judging these properties. To judge change in one patient, you need the **standard error of measurement (SEM)**, from which the **MDC** is calculated: the smallest change that is beyond measurement noise.
text.ur: **Reliability** mustaqil mizaji hai: jab kuch na badla ho (ek hi shakhs mukhtalif dinon mein, ya mukhtalif raters) to kya naap wahi jawab deta hai? **Validity** matlab ki durusti hai: kya woh wahi naapta hai jo naapne ka dawa karta hai? **Responsiveness** waqt ke saath asal tabdeeli pakadne ki salahiyat hai. **COSMIN** muhim in khasiyaton ko parakhne ke mayar tay karti hai. Ek mareez mein tabdeeli parakhne ke liye aap ko **standard error of measurement (SEM)** chahiye, jis se **MDC** nikalta hai: sab se chhoti tabdeeli jo naap ke shor se bahar ho.

text.en: Think of **a bathroom scale**. If it shows 70 kg, then 72, then 69 in a minute, it is unreliable. If it is always 5 kg too high, it is reliable but not valid. If it cannot show a 200 g change, it is not responsive enough for tiny changes. A scale needs all three. A measure with noise of 3 kg cannot tell you that you lost 1 kg.
text.ur: **Ghusal-khane ka wazan-tola** sochein. Agar ek minute mein 70, phir 72, phir 69 kg dikhaye to woh unreliable hai. Agar hamesha 5 kg zyada dikhaye to reliable lekin valid nahi. Agar 200 gram ki tabdeeli na dikha sake to chhoti tabdeeliyon ke liye kaafi responsive nahi. Tole ko teenon chahiye. 3 kg shor wala naap aap ko nahi bata sakta ke aap ka 1 kg kam hua.

title.en: Key measurement terms in plain words
title.ur: Aham naap ke alfaaz saade lafzon mein

rows.en: Agreement for continuous measures such as range of motion
rows.ur: Range of motion jaise mustaqil naap ke liye ittefaq

rows.en: Below 0.5 poor, 0.5 to 0.75 moderate, 0.75 to 0.9 good, above 0.9 excellent (a common guide)
rows.ur: 0.5 se kam kamzor, 0.5 se 0.75 darmiyani, 0.75 se 0.9 achha, 0.9 se oopar behtareen (aam rehnumai)

rows.en: Agreement beyond chance for categories such as positive or negative tests
rows.ur: Zamree jaise positive ya negative tests mein ittefaq jo ittifaq se aage ho

rows.en: Roughly 0.4 to 0.6 moderate, 0.6 to 0.8 substantial (a common guide)
rows.ur: Takreeban 0.4 se 0.6 darmiyani, 0.6 se 0.8 qabil-e-zikr (aam rehnumai)

rows.en: SEM is the typical error in a single measure; MDC is the change you need to be confident it is real
rows.ur: SEM ek naap mein aam ghalti hai; MDC woh tabdeeli hai jo asal hone ka yaqeen dilaye

rows.en: MDC at 95 percent is about 2.77 times the SEM (1.96 x square root of 2 x SEM)
rows.ur: 95 fisad par MDC takreeban SEM ka 2.77 guna hai (1.96 x square root of 2 x SEM)

rows.en: The smallest change patients feel is important
rows.ur: Sab se chhoti tabdeeli jo mareez ahem mehsoos karein

rows.en: Found by anchoring to patients' own ratings; it is about meaning, not noise
rows.ur: Mareezon ki apni rating se jodne par milti hai; yeh maani ke baare mein hai, shor ke nahi

question.en: A shoulder range of motion measure has an MDC of 10 degrees. A patient improves by 6 degrees. What can you say?
question.ur: Kandhe ki range of motion ke naap ka MDC 10 degree hai. Mareez 6 degree behtar hota hai. Aap kya keh sakte hain?

text.ur: Mareez saaf taur par behtar hua hai

feedback.en: It does not exceed the MDC.

text.en: The change is within measurement noise, so we cannot be confident it is real
text.ur: Tabdeeli naap ke shor ke andar hai, isliye yaqeen nahi ke asal hai

feedback.en: Yes — a change smaller than the MDC may be error.
feedback.ur: Haan — MDC se chhoti tabdeeli ghalti ho sakti hai.

feedback.en: The result is a small positive change.

question.en: Two therapists measure the same patient's knee extension with a goniometer and often differ by 8 degrees. Which property is low?
question.ur: Do therapists ek hi mareez ke ghutne ki extension goniometer se naapte hain aur aksar 8 degree ka farq aata hai. Kaun si khasiyat kam hai?

feedback.en: That is about detecting change over time.
feedback.ur: Yeh waqt ke saath tabdeeli pakadne ke baare mein hai.

feedback.en: That is about whether it looks appropriate.
feedback.ur: Yeh is ke baare mein hai ke munasib lagta hai ya nahi.

feedback.en: Yes — different raters do not agree.

question.en: What is the difference between MDC and MCID?
question.ur: MDC aur MCID mein kya farq hai?

text.en: MCID is always smaller than MDC
text.ur: MCID hamesha MDC se chhota hota hai

feedback.en: It can be either; both should be checked.
feedback.ur: Dono mein se koi bhi ho sakta hai; dono dekhein.

text.en: They are the same number for every test
text.ur: Har test ke liye yeh ek hi number hain

feedback.ur: Yeh alag sawalon ka jawab dete hain.

text.en: MDC is the smallest change beyond measurement error; MCID is the smallest change that patients feel is important
text.ur: MDC naap ki ghalti se aage sab se chhoti tabdeeli hai; MCID sab se chhoti tabdeeli hai jo mareez ahem mehsoos karein

feedback.en: Yes — one is statistical, the other is meaningful.
feedback.ur: Haan — ek shumariyati hai, doosri ba-maani.

text.en: **Treating any change as real change.** A one-point drop on a 10-point scale or a few degrees on a goniometer is often noise. Also, do not assume a measure is reliable because it is popular. Check whether reliability and MDC were studied in people like yours, and if a change is both beyond MDC and above the MCID, then it is both real and important.
text.ur: **Har tabdeeli ko asal tabdeeli samajhna.** 10 point scale par ek point ki kami ya goniometer par chand degree aksar shor hota hai. Yeh bhi na samjhein ke naap mashhoor hone ki wajah se reliable hai. Dekhein ke reliability aur MDC aap jaise logon mein study hue ya nahi, aur agar tabdeeli MDC se aage aur MCID se oopar ho to woh asal bhi hai aur ahem bhi.

text.en: **Make your measures steadier.** Use the same tool, the same position, the same time of day and, if possible, the same therapist. Take two or three readings and use the average. Record the method so the next visit repeats it. Small habits like these can shrink measurement error more than buying a new device.
text.ur: **Apne naap mustaqil banayein.** Wohi aala, wohi position, din ka wohi waqt aur mumkin ho to wohi therapist istemal karein. Do ya teen reading lein aur average istemal karein. Tareeqa likhein taake agli visit dohraye. Aisi chhoti aadatein naya aala khareedne se zyada naap ki ghalti kam kar sakti hain.

question.en: Why can a measure be reliable but not valid?
question.ur: Naap reliable ho kar valid kyun nahi ho sakta?

answer.en: Reliability means consistent results, not correct ones. A scale that is always 5 kg too high is perfectly reliable but wrong. Similarly, a questionnaire might give the same score every time yet fail to capture what matters to patients. Validity needs separate evidence that the numbers mean what we think.
answer.ur: Reliability ka matlab mustaqil nateeje hain, durust nahi. Jo tola hamesha 5 kg zyada dikhaye woh bilkul reliable lekin ghalat hai. Isi tarah questionnaire har baar wohi score de sakta hai lekin woh na pakde jo mareezon ke liye ahem hai. Validity ko alag saboot chahiye ke numbers ka matlab wohi hai jo hum samajhte hain.

beats.patient: A therapist uses a 10-metre walk test. The study reports an MDC of 0.18 metres per second and an MCID of 0.10 metres per second. A patient's speed rises by 0.12 metres per second.
beats.assessment: The change is above the MCID but below the MDC, so it may be meaningful to the patient but is within measurement noise for one person.
beats.treatment: She repeats the test at the next visit and uses an average of two trials, and she checks other functional measures.
beats.reassess: A larger change at the next visit exceeds the MDC, and she can say with confidence that the walking speed has really improved.

text.en: **Do not make safety decisions on a noisy measure.** A single reading of blood pressure, a small change in strength or a one-off balance score should not on its own decide whether a patient can walk unaided or return to sport. Use repeated measures and clinical judgement, and always for safety-critical decisions.
text.ur: **Shor wale naap par safety ke faisle na karein.** Blood pressure ki ek reading, taqat mein chhoti tabdeeli ya balance ka ek score akela yeh tay na kare ke mareez bina sahare chal sakta hai ya khel mein wapas ja sakta hai. Dohrayi gayi paimaishein aur clinical judgement istemal karein, aur safety ke ahem faislon ke liye hamesha.

text.en: The COSMIN checklist was developed by international consensus to assess the methodological quality of studies on measurement properties, such as reliability, validity and responsiveness. Koo and Li's guide recommends reporting the ICC model, type and definition and interpreting values with 95 percent confidence intervals, suggesting rough thresholds of below 0.5 as poor, 0.5 to 0.75 as moderate, 0.75 to 0.9 as good and above 0.9 as excellent reliability.
text.ur: COSMIN checklist beinul-aqwami ittefaq se banai gayi taake naap ki khasiyaton, jaise reliability, validity aur responsiveness, par studies ki methodological quality parkhi ja sake. Koo aur Li ki rehnumai ICC ka model, qism aur tareef report karne aur values ko 95 fisad confidence intervals ke saath parhne ki sifarish karti hai, aur takreeban hadein deti hai: 0.5 se kam kamzor, 0.5 se 0.75 darmiyani, 0.75 se 0.9 achhi aur 0.9 se oopar behtareen reliability.

text.en: **Same, True, Sensitive, Beyond noise.** Reliable (same), valid (true), responsive (sensitive to change), and a change must go beyond the noise (MDC).
text.ur: **Wahi, Sacha, Hassas, Shor se aage.** Reliable (wahi), valid (sacha), responsive (tabdeeli ke liye hassas), aur tabdeeli shor (MDC) se aage hone chahiye.

summary.en: Reliability is consistency, validity is accuracy of meaning and responsiveness is detecting change.
summary.ur: Reliability mustaqil mizaji, validity maani ki durusti aur responsiveness tabdeeli pakadna hai.

summary.en: A change must exceed the MDC to be confidently real, and exceed the MCID to matter to the patient.
summary.ur: Tabdeeli ko yaqeen se asal hone ke liye MDC se aur mareez ke liye ahem hone ke liye MCID se zyada hona chahiye.

summary.en: Standardise your measures and never make safety decisions on a single noisy reading.
summary.ur: Apne naap standard karein aur ek shor wali reading par safety ke faisle kabhi na karein.

back.en: Reliability or agreement for continuous measures.
back.ur: Mustaqil naap ke liye reliability ya ittefaq.

back.en: The smallest change beyond measurement error.
back.ur: Naap ki ghalti se aage sab se chhoti tabdeeli.

back.en: The smallest change patients feel is important.
back.ur: Sab se chhoti tabdeeli jo mareez ahem mehsoos karein.

front.en: Can a measure be reliable but invalid?
front.ur: Kya naap reliable ho kar invalid ho sakta hai?

back.en: Yes; consistent results can still be wrong.
back.ur: Haan; mustaqil nateeje phir bhi ghalat ho sakte hain.
